4. Update the solver tests that pin the metre wording (tests/film_scene_solver.test.mjs:469, 475, 521). Add a test that builds candidates at 0.5 m and 1.5 m, calls buildPickCandidateRequest, and asserts that each criterion contains a word quoted in the instructions.

title: Each shot's JEV telemetry file includes every earlier shot's and rehearsal's broker entries
description: One broker serves a whole `film shoot` (film.mjs:1056). Its telemetry ring is never cleared or partitioned, and shootOne calls dumpTelemetry(`reports/<shot>.jev.jsonl`) after each shot, which writes the entire ring. Each shot's file therefore holds all prior shots' and rehearsals' JEV calls, capped at the last 500. Per-shot JEV cost and latency analysis from these files double-counts, and a long take plus its rehearsal can push the shot's own early entries out.
failureScenario: Shot A makes 2 JEV calls, then shot B is rehearsed and shot. reports/B.jev.jsonl contains A's 2 entries plus B's. Summing costUsd per shot file overstates B's JEV spend.
evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-1000/jevprobe/ring.mjs: after 2 handler calls for A (dumped to A.jev.jsonl) and 1 for B, `B file lines: [ 0, 1, 10 ]`. Code: jev_broker.mjs:134 `const ring = []` (no reset API); shoot.mjs:326-328 dumps the whole ring per shot.
suggestedFix: Add `broker.clearTelemetry()` (or `mark()` returning an index / `telemetrySince(mark)`) and call it at the start of each shot and rehearsal. Alternatively, dump only the entries recorded since that shot started.
fixes:
Mark-and-filter fix in jev_broker.mjs, which avoids clearing shared state:
- Keep a running counter `let recorded = 0;` and stamp each entry in record(): `entry.n = recorded++` (or track how many entries have been dropped).
- Expose `telemetryMark() { return recorded; }`.
- Let `dumpTelemetry(file, {since} = {})` write only `ring.filter(e => since == null || e.n >= since)`.

In shoot.mjs shootOne:
- Take `const mark = o.broker?.telemetryMark?.()` once, before the attempt loop. The shot's file then still holds its own rehearsal and all of its retakes.
- Call `o.broker.dumpTelemetry(path.join(paths.reports, `${shotId}.jev.jsonl`), { since: mark })`.

Also update the shoot.mjs step-8 comment and the broker header to say the dump is per shot. Add a 2-shot case to tests/film_cli_session.test.mjs (S5e-style with `--all`) asserting that b.jev.jsonl has only b's rows.

title: --jev-max-usd-per-hour is enforced per CLI process, so the hourly window starts empty on every `film` invocation
description: makeJev creates a new createJevClient per command context. The client's minute and hour windows are in-memory (jev.mjs createWindow), and `film run` even copies ctx per step (`{...ctx, args}`), giving each step its own client. Every `film shoot --shot=…` or `film rehearse` therefore starts with an empty hour window. When the director iterates shot by shot or retakes through separate invocations, total JEV spend in an hour is bounded by invocations × cap, not by the cap. SPEC §5 presents these as budget caps per hour.
failureScenario: The director runs `film rehearse` and `film shoot --shot=X` for 10 shots within an hour, each as its own process. Each process may spend up to $2 before refusing, so the effective cap is about $20/h, not $2/h.
evidence: film.mjs:256-275 `makeJev` → `deps.createJevClient({... budget: {maxUsdPerHour, maxCallsPerMin}})` per ctx; film.mjs:1222 `COMMANDS[name].run({ ...ctx, args: ... })`; jev.mjs:745-746 `minuteCalls = createWindow(MINUTE_MS); hourCost = createWindow(HOUR_MS)` (memory only).
suggestedFix: Persist the rolling spend: append (t, costUsd) to a small ledger under ~/.config/holtburger-film/ or the project dir, load it into hourCost at client creation, and append on each successful call. At minimum, document that the cap applies per invocation.

title: Each pilot request carries ~10.6 KB of criteria, about 6–10× the cost assumption, so the default $2/h cap binds below the SPEC's 3–8 decisions/s
description: research_jev.md and pilot_design.md estimate pilot cost as ~500-token states × 5 Hz ≈ $0.38/h. The state is small (≈1.26 KB), but every request re-sends the full question set: maneuver 5.4 KB, framing 2.0 KB, occluder 1.7 KB, risk 0.8 KB and subject_lost 0.6 KB, for an 11.9 KB payload. The client's own pre-flight estimate (jev.mjs estimateInput: per-question passes at 3 bytes/token) is 5,620 tokens, or $0.000236 per call: $4.25/h at decisionHz 5 and $6.8/h at 8 Hz. Even at 4 bytes/token billed once (≈3k tokens) it is ≈ $2.3/h at 5 Hz. With the default --jev-max-usd-per-hour=2, sustained realtime consulting (dungeon corridors keep 'obstacle-near' true) hits budget refusals. After that the pilot flies codePolicy for the rest of the rolling hour.
failureScenario: About 50 minutes of realtime shooting in corridors with the pilot consulting at about 5 Hz. The hour spend passes $2, every later decide() throws JevError 'budget', and the pilot silently becomes code-only for the remaining takes in that window.
evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-1000/jevprobe/size.mjs (buildPilotState + questionsFor({hasSubject:true}), 300-char standing order): `payload bytes 11918`, per-question bytes maneuver 5382 / risk 807 / subject_lost 622 / occluder_action 1720 / framing 2030, `state bytes 1259 est tokens(cost) 5620`, `est $/call 0.000236 $/h @5Hz 4.25 @8Hz 6.80`. Default cap film.mjs:266 `numArg(args, "jev-max-usd-per-hour", 2…)`.
suggestedFix: Trim the criteria. The maneuver question restates its definitions in every option; define BLOCKED, RISE-OK and the other terms once and keep option texts short. Also ask framing and occluder_action only when their consult reason fired, not on every consult. Separately, re-derive the cost estimate in SPEC and research from real request sizes, and either raise the default cap or size decisionHz so the default budget covers sustained use.

title: Stepped takes run as one unbroken microtask chain, so rAF-driven subsystems never advance between film frames
description: step() calls `window.__renderOnce(ts)`, and index.js tick finishes in a microtask: under the default `?syncPhysicsTick` there is one `await Promise.resolve()` hop, and postRender resolves the step promise. take_player.runStepped then goes straight on to sense → `pilot.tickStepped` → poseStep → the next step(). `tickStepped` resolves without a macrotask when no JEV call is due (code mode or reused answer), and `recorder.waitForCapacity()` returns at once while `hasCapacity()` holds. Nothing in the loop yields to the event loop. So every subsystem paced by its own requestAnimationFrame stays frozen for the whole take, or moves only in bursts. This covers: animated_scenery's wind driver (seam 7 `setSceneryTimeSource` cannot work, because the driver only reads the film clock from its own rAF and clamps dt to 0.1 s); the statics.js `_bbLoop` billboard LOD leaves (far trees keep facing the previous camera direction); the xu7 texture drain; and the statics `_spLoop` static-particle tick when `particleClock=off`. The CLI's CDP `recorder.drain` calls cannot interleave either, and encoder output callbacks pile up until a yield. In a rehearse nothing yields at all. In a shoot the chain yields only when the encoder queue goes above `maxQueue` (8).
failureScenario: CLI shoot of a drone flyover over trees (the CLI boots with particleClock=sim). With the 1070 hardware encoder, waitForCapacity sleeps about every 8–13 frames. Tree sway updates only on those yields, at ~0.1 s of sway per 13 frames (≈25% speed, stepped). Billboard tree cards snap orientation every ~13 frames while the camera moves. In a rehearse they never update.
evidence: film_clock.js:398 `const ok = render(ts);` → index.js tick (`await syncTickHop()` = `await Promise.resolve()`) → `_postRenderStreamSlot()` → `liveScene3dRef?.film?.postRender?.()` → film_clock onPostRender `p.resolve()`. take_player.js:1192-1205 `const out = await R.pilot.tickStepped(...)` … `await renderStep(...)` … `if (typeof R.recorder.waitForCapacity === "function") await R.recorder.waitForCapacity();` (returns immediately when hasCapacity). pilot.js:708 tickStepped = `chain.then(run, run)` (no timer). Executed: a scratch copy of the tests/film_api.test.mjs harness, with `__renderOnce` changed to postRender after a microtask hop (as index.js does), ran the REAL installFilmMode → prepare(dolly, 4 s, 30 fps, pilot code) → rehearse. Output: `rehearse ok=true frames=120 renders=129 event-loop turns during the take=1 16ms-timer callbacks=0`. Independent rAF loops in the client: animated_scenery.js:1313, statics.js:4660 (_bbLoop) and 5793 (_spLoop), xu7_textures.js:267.
suggestedFix: Yield one animation frame per film frame inside film_clock.step(). Order: set `st.clockMs` to the upcoming ts (the camera pose for the frame is already written by take_player), then `await new Promise(r => win.requestAnimationFrame(() => r()))` with a setTimeout fallback (~50 ms) for throttled pages, then compute or re-base ts against `frameTs()`, then call `render(ts)`. On the FIRST step, cancel the pending realtime re-arm before the wait so no wall-clock tick runs during it, for example by issuing the explicit-ts cancel path first or by having begin() trigger the `_cancelSchedule` seam. The existing 15 s step timeout covers a rAF that never fires. Then the scenery driver, billboards and texture drains run exactly once per film frame on the film clock, and CDP drains interleave.
fixes:
Make each stepped frame run the client's rAF-paced work exactly once, on the film clock.

Option A (keeps the existing modules, close to the suggested fix): in `film_clock.step()`, after computing `ts` and setting `st.clockMs = ts`, wait for one animation frame before calling `render(ts)`:

`await new Promise(r => { let done = false; const fin = () => { if (!done) { done = true; r(); } }; win.requestAnimationFrame?.(fin); setT?.(fin, 50); })`

- Make `step()` an async wrapper that keeps the `FILM_CLOCK_BUSY` / `inflight` bookkeeping.
- Cancel the realtime loop's pending re-arm before the first wait, so no wall-clock `tick` runs during it. Either `begin()` calls a new index.js seam that exposes `_cancelSchedule`, or `__renderOnce` gains a no-render cancel mode.
- After the wait, re-check `frameTs()` against `st.lastTs` (the existing re-base logic) before rendering.
- Network, encoder output callbacks and the CLI's `recorder.drain` then interleave every frame.

Option B (deterministic, no wall-clock dependence; can be combined with A):
- Export a single-iteration driver from animated_scenery (the body of `loop`, taking dt) and call it with `1/fps` from a film `preFrame` listener while a stepped take is active. Suppress the private rAF while the scenery time source is set, so it does not double-advance.
- Call `tickStaticsBillboards(live)` from the same `preFrame` listener after the camera pose is written.
- Pass both through the `installFilmMode` deps from `scene3d/index.js`, which already imports both modules.
- Keep a `setTimeout(0)` / MessageChannel yield per step for the network, encoder and CDP interleave.

In both cases, add a test to `tests/film_api.test.mjs` that asserts at least one macrotask turn runs per stepped frame during `rehearse`.

Yield one animation frame per film frame inside `film_clock.step()`, before rendering:

1. Set `st.clockMs = <upcoming ts>` first, so the private rAF drivers read the new film time.
2. Then await `win.requestAnimationFrame` with a ~50 ms `setTimeout` fallback for throttled or occluded pages. The existing 15 s step timeout still covers a rAF that never fires.
3. Only after the wait, compute `ts`, the frame number and the rebase from `frameTs()`. A pending realtime re-arm from before the hold could fire during the very first wait, and the existing rebase logic then moves `base` past that frame. Alternatively, call the explicit-ts cancel path (`_cancelSchedule`) at `begin()`.
4. Then call `render(ts)`.

Result: the scenery driver (dt = 1/fps, never clamped), the billboard orientation and the texture drains each run exactly once per film frame on the film clock, and CDP drains interleave every frame. Cost is at most one vsync of wall time per frame, small next to a 30-45 ms render on the 1070.

The alternative is to inject `tickAnimatedScenery` and `tickStaticsBillboards` from scene3d/index.js into the `installFilmMode` deps and call them from `film.preFrame`. That alternative also has to stop the private rAF loops from adding a second advance at yields: suppress them while `holdLoop` is set, or have them read a film dt of 0.

title: With ?particleClock=sim (the CLI boot default) begin() jumps the particle clock forward by the accumulated sim lag, killing every live particle at frame 0
description: installSources() feeds time_rng `setCurrentTime(() => st.clockMs / 1000)`, where clockMs is a performance.now()-based frame timestamp. Under `?particleClock=sim`, which tools/film/lib/session.mjs always puts in the boot URL, emitters and PhysicsScript queues hold timestamps in the SIM base `liveScene3d._particleSimNowS`. loop.js advances that base only by the clamped dt (`min(prev + dt, wall)`), so it lags wall time permanently: every hitch over 0.1 s and every dt-recovery freeze adds to the lag. At begin() the particle clock therefore jumps forward by (wall − sim). Particle lifetimes are computed from `now - lastUpdateTime` (particle.js:478-488), so every live particle dies on the first stepped frame. `totalSeconds` emitters stop (`creationTime + totalSeconds < currentTime()`), and queued script hooks fire together. After a take, restoreSources sets `_particleSimNowS = film`, which is ≈ wall at begin plus the film duration. A stepped take renders slower than real time, so the lag grows by (wall duration − film duration) with every take, and each later take jumps further. The 0.25 s default pre-roll cannot refill emitters that re-emit at most one particle per update.
failureScenario: Shooting a brazier or chimney-smoke shot as the second take of a session: the previous 10 s take took ~60 s of wall time, so the jump is ≈50 s. At frame 0 all smoke and fire particles vanish together and regrow one particle per frame through the first seconds of the recorded take.
evidence: film_clock.js:256 `const secFn = () => st.clockMs / 1000;` and :258 `timeRng.setCurrentTime(secFn)`; begin() :319 `st.base = ft` (frameTime.tsMs, the wall base) while :324 detects simMode but uses it only in restoreSources (:280-285). index.js:5502-5503 `liveScene3d._particleSimNowS = performance.now() / 1000; setCurrentTime(() => liveScene3d._particleSimNowS);`. loop.js:3354 `scene3d._particleSimNowS = Math.min((scene3d._particleSimNowS ?? _pcNowMs / 1000) + dt, _pcNowMs / 1000)`. session.mjs:62 `...&particleClock=sim&...`. Executed a scratch script with the real createFilmClock (timeRng.particleClockMode()==='sim', _particleSimNowS=100, frameTime.tsMs=160000): `particle currentTime() before begin: 100` / `particle currentTime() at film frame 0: 160.033 → jump of 60.033 s`.
suggestedFix: In begin(), when simMode, capture `simBase = live._particleSimNowS` and install `setCurrentTime(() => simBase + (st.clockMs - st.base) / 1000)`, so particle time advances by exactly the film time from the sim clock's current value. In restoreSources, set `_particleSimNowS = max(current, simBase + filmElapsed)`. Keep the ts/1000 base only for `particleClock=off`, whose emitters are wall-based. Add a film_clock unit test with simMode on and _particleSimNowS ≠ frameTime.tsMs/1000 that asserts there is no jump.
fixes:
In begin(), capture the sim clock and run the film particle time on it.
- Set `st.simBase = st.simMode && Number.isFinite(live._particleSimNowS) ? live._particleSimNowS : null` and `st.base0 = st.base`.
- In installSources, install `timeRng.setCurrentTime(st.simBase !== null ? () => st.simBase + (st.clockMs - st.base0) / 1000 : () => st.clockMs / 1000)`.
- Use base0, not st.base, because step() re-bases st.base when a realtime frame slips in.
- In restoreSources for simMode, compute `filmEnd = st.simBase + (st.clockMs - st.base0) / 1000` and set `live._particleSimNowS = Math.max(live._particleSimNowS, filmEnd)` when finite, else filmEnd. Then reinstall `() => live._particleSimNowS`.
- Keep the wall base (`clockMs/1000`) only for particleClock=off/loop, whose emitters are wall-based.
- fx and scenery time sources stay on the ms wall base.
- Add a K1-style test in tests/film_runtime_camera.test.mjs: simMode on, `_particleSimNowS` set well below `frameTime.tsMs/1000`. Assert that the time read at film frame 0 equals simBase + 1/fps (no jump) and that end() leaves `_particleSimNowS` at or above simBase + filmElapsed.

In film_clock.js:
- In `begin()`, after computing `st.simMode`, record `st.base0 = st.base` (this value is not changed by `step()` rebases). Also record `st.simBase = st.simMode && Number.isFinite(live._particleSimNowS) ? live._particleSimNowS : null`.
- Change `installSources` so the time source is `secFn = st.simBase !== null ? () => st.simBase + (st.clockMs - st.base0) / 1000 : () => st.clockMs / 1000`. Particle time then continues from the sim clock's current value and advances by exactly the film time. A `step()` rebase only adds the length of the one realtime frame that slipped in, so it stays continuous.
- In `restoreSources()` sim mode, compute `film = st.simBase !== null ? st.simBase + (st.clockMs - st.base0) / 1000 : st.clockMs / 1000` and keep the existing rule: if `_particleSimNowS` is behind it, set it to `film`. The sim clock then never moves past the film time.
- Leave `particleClock=off` on the existing `ts/1000` wall base, because those emitters run on wall time.
- Add a film_clock unit test that turns sim mode on with `_particleSimNowS` (for example 100) different from `frameTime.tsMs/1000` (for example 160). It should assert that `currentTime()` at film frame 0 is about `100 + 1/fps`, not about 160. It should also assert that after `end()` the value is `_particleSimNowS ≥ 100 + film duration` and has not been pushed toward wall time.

In `scene3d/film/runtime/film_clock.js`, run the particle clock on the sim base whenever `simMode` is on.

1. In `begin()`, compute `simMode` before `installSources`. When `simMode` is on and `Number.isFinite(live._particleSimNowS)`, set `st.simS = live._particleSimNowS`.
2. In `installSources`, install `timeRng.setCurrentTime(() => st.simS)` in sim mode. Keep `secFn = st.clockMs/1000` only for `particleClock=off/loop`, whose emitters hold wall timestamps.
3. In `step()`, advance `st.simS += dt` using the `dt` already computed from `ts - st.lastTs`. Accumulating per step stays correct across a re-base, unlike `clockMs - base`.
4. In `restoreSources`, set `live._particleSimNowS = Math.max(live._particleSimNowS, st.simS)` and do not write the wall-based film time there.

Do not rely on `loop.js` advancing `_particleSimNowS` during the take. Its `min(prev + dt, wall)` cap would slow particles down whenever steps render faster than real time.

Add a K1-style test in `tests/film_runtime_camera.test.mjs`:
- Set up: `particleClockMode` returns `'sim'`, `_particleSimNowS = 0.9`, `frameTime.tsMs = 1000`.
- Assert the particle time at step 0 is 0.9 + 1/30, i.e. no jump.
- Assert that after `end()` the sim clock is ≥ 0.9 + frames/30.
- Run a second take after advancing wall time and assert it does not jump either.

title: Pilot 'fade' does nothing for the main soft occluders (trees and props): static and scenery hits carry no id and nothing sets the statics __filmHidden seam
description: sense_words.js OCCLUDER_CLASSES classifies soft = ['tree','prop','particles'], and policy_code / the JEV criteria map soft occluders to `fade` ('the film runtime can fade them out'). world_query.describeHit returns `guid` only for the entities/objects layers. For the scenery/statics/buildingMesh layers it returns `{kind, did}` with `guid: null`, so sensors.js occluderIds has no entry for a tree or rock, and mapper occluderIds() yields `fadeIds = []`. take_player.fade() handles only numeric entity guids (setFilmHidden) and string particle keys. The statics seam `userData.__filmHidden` (SPEC §4.4, statics.js cullStaticsGroup) has no caller anywhere in scene3d/film, and BatchedMesh scenery would need setVisibleAt. Because the choice is 'fade' and not 'reroute', the camera also never takes the reroute bias for these occluders. The subject stays hidden behind the tree for the whole commit window or longer.
failureScenario: An orbit around an NPC behind a tree trunk. Sensors report `occluded_by: tree`, and the code policy (or JEV) answers occluder_action 'fade'. sp.fadeIds is [], so take_player.fade returns immediately. The take is recorded with the subject mostly hidden (report.obstruction.framesHidden > 0) and no fade or reroute ever happens.
evidence: sense_words.js:208-212 `soft: ["tree", "prop", "particles"], solid: [...]`. policy_code.js:169 `if (cls === "soft") return { choice: "fade", ...}`. world_query.js:899-907 (statics branch sets `did` only, `guid` stays null). sensors.js:743 `if (rec.guid !== null && !occIds.includes(rec.guid)) occIds.push(rec.guid);`. mapper.js:488 `sp.fadeIds = occChoice === "fade" ? occluderIds(sf, limits.maxFadeIds) : [];`. take_player.js:759-792 fade() handles only `typeof id === "number"` (entity) and string particle keys. `rg '__filmHidden' scene3d/film` has no match outside comments.
suggestedFix: Have describeHit return a static handle (the staticsNearCached record's node plus instance id) and carry it in subject.occluderIds, for example as `{static: key}`. In take_player.fade, set `node.userData.__filmHidden = true` and `node.visible = false` for Mesh/InstancedMesh/LOD, and `setVisibleAt(id, false)` for BatchedMesh, recording the previous state; restore it in restoreFades. Until that exists, move 'tree' and 'prop' to the solid class (reroute), so neither the policy nor the JEV criteria picks a no-op.
fixes: Minimal v1 fix in scene3d/film/pilot/mapper.js around line 488: `const ids = occChoice === "fade" ? occluderIds(sf, limits.maxFadeIds) : []; sp.fadeIds = ids; sp.reroute = occChoice === "reroute" || (occChoice === "fade" && ids.length === 0);`. A fade that cannot be applied then falls back to the reroute bias instead of doing nothing. Optionally, also make take_player treat "fade asked but nothing actually hidden" as reroute, which covers entity and particle ids that fail to resolve. A later fix that makes static fades actually work: have describeHit return the placement handle (`{lbKey, index, source, did}` from the staticsNearCached row), carry it in subject.occluderIds as an object, and add a resolver from that placement to its staticsGroup node and instance. That means setting `userData.__filmHidden = true` and `visible = false` on Mesh/InstancedMesh/LOD singletons, or calling `setVisibleAt(instanceId, false)` for BatchedMesh, recording the previous state and restoring it in restoreFades. Until that resolver exists, the questions.js occluder text should not promise that trees and props can be faded.

Minimal v1 fix, in scene3d/film/pilot/mapper.js apply(): when occChoice === "fade" and occluderIds(sf, max) is empty, fall back to reroute. Concretely: `const ids = occChoice === "fade" ? occluderIds(sf, limits.maxFadeIds) : []; sp.fadeIds = ids; sp.reroute = occChoice === "reroute" || (occChoice === "fade" && ids.length === 0);`. Also count the fallback in counters so the report shows it.

Optionally, move 'tree' and 'prop' out of OCCLUDER_CLASSES.soft, or narrow the soft wording in questions.js, so JEV is no longer told that the runtime can fade trees and statics.

The fuller fix, if wanted later: describeHit returns a static handle (node plus instance id) for the statics/scenery layers. take_player.fade sets `userData.__filmHidden = true` plus `visible = false` only on singleton Mesh/LOD nodes, and uses setVisibleAt(id, false) for BatchedMesh, saving the previous state and restoring it in restoreFades. InstancedMesh scenery should not be node-hidden, because that hides every instance; for those, use the reroute fallback.

title: Fog looks restart the ~20 s wall-clock roll-in on every prepare and are mid-transition during stepped takes
description: look.fog.set always stores a FRESH object: `win.__environFogOverride = lookFogOverride(v)`. environ_override.js treats a new object identity as a new AdminEnvirons message and resets `transition = 0` (the fog snaps back to the day fog). It then steps the transition on wall-clock fog ticks (0.8 s) and light ticks (15 s), about 20 s of wall time in total. prepare() re-applies the take's whole look on every shot, so even consecutive shots with the same `fog` restart the roll-in. Because the ticks run on performance.now() and not on film time, a stepped take renders an arbitrary, non-repeatable part of the transition, depending on render speed. Nothing waits for `transition >= 1` before shooting.
failureScenario: A plan with defaults.look.fog = 'white'. Each prepare(take) → look.apply → a new override object, and the fog resets to clear. shoot() starts immediately, so the first seconds of every take show fog rolling in. A locked replay of the same take shows a different fog density, because the transition follows wall time.
evidence: look.js:211-215 `set(v) { ... const o = lookFogOverride(v); win.__environFogOverride = o; ...}` (lookFogOverride returns `{ option: opt, ...LOOK_FOG_ROWS[opt] }`, a new object every call). environ_override.js:196-199 `sync(o) { if ((o || null) !== source) set(o); ...}` with set() → `transition = 0`. fogTick() uses `now()` = retail_light_tick.js:58 `performance.now() * 0.001`. loop.js:1375 exposes `window.__environOverrideState()` (with `transition`), which film code never reads.
suggestedFix: In handlers.fog.set, keep the current `win.__environFogOverride` object when its `option` already matches, and only assign a new object when the fog really changes. In prepare/shoot (or as a `look.ready()` that the CLI awaits), poll `window.__environOverrideState().transition >= 1` (and `lightT >= 1`) with a timeout before recording. Alternatively, add a film-only seam on the environ override that sets the transition to 1 for takes.
fixes:
(a) In look.js handlers.fog.set, reuse the current override when it already has the requested fog: `const cur = win.__environFogOverride; if (o && cur && cur.option === o.option && cur.fogRgb === o.fogRgb) return {ok:true, value:o.name};`. A look with the same fog then no longer restarts the fade on each prepare or rehearse. Update the test at film_runtime_world.test.mjs:150-152 to match.

(b) Make the fog fully in before recording, in a deterministic way. Film code may not import environ_override.js, so add a film-only seam on the loop side, e.g. `window.__environOverrideSettle = () => { environOverride.settle(); retailLightTick.invalidate(); }`. Here settle() is a new method on createEnvironOverride that sets transition = fogT = 1 and resets nextFogTick, and invalidate() makes the next light tick latch the ambient at t = 1. Inject this seam through installFilmMode deps, and have look.fog.set call it when present.

Fallback: have prepare (or a look.ready() that the CLI awaits) poll `window.__environOverrideState()` until both `fogT >= 1` and `lightT >= 1`, with a timeout of about 25 s. Then report the fog as unsettled in the take report, not as silently partial.

1. In `look.js` `handlers.fog.set`, reuse the current object when the fog has not changed: `const cur = win.__environFogOverride; if (o && cur && cur.option === o.option && Number.isFinite(cur.fogRgb)) return { ok: true, value: o.name, kept: true }; win.__environFogOverride = o;`. Update `tests/film_runtime_world.test.mjs` L1 (lines 150-152) so it asserts the identity is kept for the same fog and replaced for a different one.
2. Make sure a take never starts mid-fade. Add a film-only settle seam: in `environ_override.js`, add a `settle()` method that sets `transition = 1` and `fogT = 1`, and latches `amb` at t = 1 when an override is active. Expose it from `loop.js` beside `__environOverrideState`, for example `window.__environOverrideSettle = () => environOverride.settle()`. Then have `look.js` (or `index.js` prepare, after `look.apply`) call it when fog is set, and follow it with `relight()` so the ambient lights on the next frame.
3. Fallback if no seam is added: in `prepare()`/`shoot()`, poll `window.__environOverrideState()` until `transition >= 1 && lightT >= 1`, with a ~25 s timeout, before recording. Report a warning on timeout. The loop must still be running while this waits.

title: Realtime takes record one frame per display refresh, but the CLI muxes and times them at the take's constant fps
description: runRealtime() arms a grab (`R.armed = { t }`) on EVERY requestAnimationFrame callback and pushes a table row per callback. The recorder stamps wall time, so the frames are variable-rate at the display or GPU rate (22–31 fps measured on the 1070 at mid, up to 60 Hz on light scenes). The CLI stream-copies the raw Annex-B with a constant `-r <fps>` (ffmpeg.mjs:130) and reports `durationSec: raw.frames / fps` (shoot.mjs:310), so the clip's speed and length are wrong unless the display rate is exactly `fps`. Realtime is the mode used for moving NPC/avatar subjects.
failureScenario: A 10 s realtime take of a walking NPC at fps=30 on the 1070 at 1080p renders ~24 fps, giving ~240 frames. Muxed at 30 fps it plays in 8 s: the NPC walks 25% fast and the take no longer fits its timeline slot or the song beats. On a light scene at 60 Hz, ~600 frames play at half speed.
evidence: take_player.js:1300-1311 in onFrame: `if (R.armed) R.dropped += 1; ... else { R.armed = { t }; }` runs on every rAF callback, with no frame-boundary check against R.fps. recorder.js grab() stamps `Math.round(t * 1e6)`. tools/film/lib/ffmpeg.mjs:130 `-r <fps> -i take.h264 -c copy`. tools/film/lib/shoot.mjs:310 `durationSec: raw.frames / fps`.
suggestedFix: In runRealtime, sample the realtime run onto the film grid: keep `nextK`, and when wall `t >= nextK/fps` arm a grab stamped `nextK/fps` and advance nextK. Skip display frames that fall between grid points. When a frame interval covers more than one grid point, grab the same canvas again with the following timestamp(s) so the stream stays constant-rate. Alternatively, have the CLI mux with the per-frame timestamps (VFR mp4) and compute duration from them, not from frames/fps.
fixes:
Put realtime takes on the film grid in the page, so the stream really is constant-rate.

In `runRealtime`, keep a counter `nextK`. On each rAF callback, after `poseStep`, compute `n = floor(t * R.fps + 1e-6) - nextK + 1`:
- If `n <= 0`, do not arm a grab (skip this display frame).
- Otherwise, arm `R.armed = { t: nextK / R.fps, count: n }` and advance `nextK += n`.

In `installGrab`, call `R.recorder.grab(a.t + j / R.fps)` for `j` in `0 .. a.count-1`, all inside the same postRender. VideoFrame-from-canvas is synchronous there, so a repeated grab encodes the same drawn frame again with the next timestamp.

Keep the dropped and over-capacity accounting per grid frame, and cap the duplicates with the existing `hasCapacity()` check. The drained frame count then equals about takeDuration × fps, so `-r fps` stream copy, `durationSec = frames / fps` and the frame-indexed EDL trims are all correct.

Fallback, as a CLI-only alternative: write the per-chunk `timestampUs` into an ffconcat or mkvmerge timecode file and mux variable-rate. Compute durationSec from `lastTimestampUs - firstTimestampUs + 1/fps`, and resample to constant fps (`-vf fps=<fps>`) before the frame-indexed EDL trims.

Fix this on the page side so that every consumer (the drain, `-r fps`, the EDL frame math, plannedFrames, and the rows table and locked replay) stays at a constant rate:

1. In runRealtime, keep `nextK = 0`.
2. In onFrame, after poseStep, find the grid points this frame covers: n = number of k with k/R.fps <= t (that is, `while (nextK / R.fps <= t + 1e-9)`), capped so that nextK stays below round(D·fps).
3. If n == 0, skip this display frame. Do not arm a grab and do not count it as dropped.
4. If n >= 1, arm `R.armed = { ts: [nextK/R.fps, ..., (nextK+n-1)/R.fps] }` and advance nextK by n.
5. In installGrab, call `R.recorder.grab(ti)` once for each stamp, inside the same postRender. The same canvas can be wrapped in a VideoFrame more than once, and this repeats the frame when the display runs slower than fps.
6. Push table rows on the same grid, so `rows.length == frames` and locked replays line up.
7. Report `durationSec` as frames / fps. That is now correct, because the frames are on the grid.

An alternative, CLI-only fix: write the per-chunk timestamps the drain already receives into a timecode or concat file, mux as variable frame rate, then re-encode with `-vf fps=<fps>` (no stream copy). Take the duration from lastTimestampUs, not from frames/fps. The page-side grid is the simpler fix and needs no change to edl.mjs.

title: In the default film boot (no ?clouds=on) depth of field blurs the pre-aerial-perspective scene, so defocused backgrounds lose their haze
description: Owner decision: DoF ships in v1, and the CLI boot always adds filmDof=on. But buildFilmUrl does not select the split chain (`?clouds=on`), so the DoF is appended to the legacy single fxPass. pmndrs effects build their blur buffers in update() from the pass INPUT. So the far-blur colour the DoF mixes in is the scene before this pass's AerialPerspective/horizonDissolve, while in-focus pixels keep the haze. The SSAO composite (attribute NONE) also sorts after the DoF and is applied sharp over the blur. SEAMS.md documents this caveat and recommends clouds=on for film, but the runtime and boot never apply that recommendation.
failureScenario: Default CLI shoot, classic.rack-focus or a shallow `look.dof` from a character to distant hills. The defocused hills are blurred but un-hazed (darker and more saturated than the in-focus haze), and AO contact darkening stays crisp inside the blurred background.
evidence: atmosphere_pipeline.js:1748-1754 legacy chain `fxPass = new EffectPass(camera, ...[heatHaze, fxDistort, ssaoComposite, ..., aerialPerspective, horizonDissolve, ...], ...(filmDof ? [filmDof.effect] : []))`. The pipeline's own note (:855-861) says 'the defocused colour there is the scene before this pass's aerial perspective / horizon dissolve ... and the AO composite (attribute NONE) lands after it'. tools/film/lib/session.mjs:59-62 boot query has no `clouds=on`. pmndrs 6.39.1 DepthOfFieldEffect.update: `this.maskPass.render(renderer, inputBuffer, renderTargetMasked)` / `bokehNearBasePass.render(renderer, inputBuffer, ...)`.
suggestedFix: Either add `clouds=on` to buildFilmUrl, since the split chain defocuses the finished atmosphere, or, when filmDof is on, split the legacy fxPass at horizonDissolve the same way the split chain does: PostChainTargetPass with the atmosphere effects, then a PostChainSourcePass with [DoF, fxGlow, lensFlare, bloom, …]. Then the DoF input is post-aerial and post-AO.

title: begin() followed by end() with no step() leaves two requestAnimationFrame chains (render loop ticks twice per frame from then on)
description: begin() sets holdLoop but does not cancel the realtime loop's already-pending rAF; only the first explicit-ts `__renderOnce(ts)` does (`_cancelSchedule()`). end() always clears holdLoop and calls a bare `__renderOnce()` to 're-arm', and that tick's scheduleNext arms a NEW rAF. If no step ran and no task boundary passed, the old pending rAF is still queued and now fires with holdLoop cleared, so it re-arms too. The result is two permanent chains: every frame runs tick() twice, doubling CPU and GPU cost for the rest of the session and halving later realtime-take frame rates. Reachable paths: __film.abort() while the recorder is starting (runStepped: begin → `if (abortRequested) break` at pre-roll i=0 → finally end()); preRollStep throwing at i=0 (writePose FILM_CAMERA_WRITE); scout stills where every candidate write is rejected.
failureScenario: The CLI times out a shoot and calls __film.abort() while `await rec.start()` (isConfigSupported) is pending. runStepped begins and immediately breaks, and end() re-arms. From then on the page renders twice per vsync until reload.
evidence: film_clock.js:340 `hooks.holdLoop = true;` (no cancel); :456-461 `hooks.holdLoop = false; ... render();` (bare re-arm); index.js:3061-3062 `if (explicitTs && liveScene3dRef?.film?.holdLoop) _cancelSchedule();` (only explicit steps cancel); scheduleNext `_schedRafId = requestAnimationFrame(tick)` overwrites the id without cancelling. Executed a scratch script that lifts `_cancelSchedule`/`scheduleNext`/`window.__renderOnce` verbatim from scene3d/index.js, with one pending rAF, plus the REAL createFilmClock: begin({fps:30}) then end(). Output: `display frame 0: 2 rAF callbacks → 2 ticks` (same for frames 1 and 2).
suggestedFix: In end(), re-arm only when the realtime chain is actually dead. If no stepped frame ran and `frameTs()` has not advanced past `st.base` (no realtime tick ran during the hold), the pre-hold rAF is still queued: just clear holdLoop and skip the bare `__renderOnce()`. Otherwise re-arm. Alternatively, make the index.js re-arm idempotent with an explicit option (e.g. `__renderOnce(undefined, {rearm:true})` calling `_cancelSchedule()` first) used only by the film clock.
fixes:
Make the film re-arm idempotent at the seam, so flag-off behaviour stays unchanged. In scene3d/index.js `window.__renderOnce`, cancel any pending re-arm on a bare call while film hooks are installed:

```js
const explicitTs = Number.isFinite(tsMs);
if (liveScene3dRef?.film && (!explicitTs || liveScene3dRef.film.holdLoop)) _cancelSchedule();
```

The bare `__renderOnce()` from `end()` then always leaves exactly one chain, whether or not the pre-hold rAF is still queued. With film off, `liveScene3dRef.film` is never set, so harness behaviour is unchanged. Update the SEAMS.md and index.js comments to match.

Alternative, film-local only: in film_clock.js `end()`, skip the bare `render()` when `st.frame < 0` and `frameTs() === st.base`. That means no step ran and no realtime tick passed during the hold, so the pre-hold re-arm is still pending; just clear `holdLoop`. This is weaker: it misses a tick that is mid-hop under `syncPhysicsTick`.

Add a unit test with a fake rAF queue: `begin()` then `end()` with no step must leave exactly one pending rAF, and a normal stepped take must also leave exactly one.

Make the hand-back re-arm idempotent on the index.js side, so it works whether or not a step ran.

1. In scene3d/index.js, change the signature to `window.__renderOnce = (tsMs, opts) => {...}` and add:
   `if (!explicitTs && opts && opts.rearm === true) _cancelSchedule();`
   This sits next to the existing explicit-ts cancel. Flag off: no caller passes opts, so behaviour is byte-identical.

2. In film_clock.js end(), call `render(undefined, { rearm: true })` instead of `render()`. The pre-hold rAF or pacer timeout still pending in the zero-step case is then cancelled before the re-arming tick arms the one new chain.

Alternative that only touches film_clock.js: at begin(), store `st.heldFrameTs = frameTs()`. In end(), skip the bare re-arm when `st.frame < 0 && frameTs() === st.heldFrameTs`, meaning no step and no realtime tick ran during the hold, so the pre-hold re-arm is still queued and will resume the loop. Still clear holdLoop in that case. The index.js option is more robust because it also cleans up any leftover second chain.

Add a film_hooks/film_runtime_camera test: start with one pending rAF, call begin() then end() with no step, and assert exactly one pending rAF afterwards.

title: A smoke cloud that the pilot faded can stay hidden after the take (safety restores its stale 'previous' value last)
description: In poseStep, fade() runs before safety.clamp(). Both look up emitters through the same per-frame particles_query snapshot (cached on frameTime.tsMs and built before the fade). So in the frame where the pilot first fades cloud E, and E is also within the lens radius, safety.updateLens still sees E: it records `{prev: true, hadOwn: true}` (the fade's value) and sets filmHidden again. execute()'s finally restores in the wrong order. restoreFades() first deletes E.filmHidden, then safety.release() writes back `prev = true`, leaving E hidden in the live client after the take and in every later take.
failureScenario: An FPV push through a smoke cloud that is also the subject's occluder. The pilot answers 'fade' while the eye is within 1 m of the cloud, and the take ends with the eye still within 2 m of it. After the take the brazier's smoke stays invisible until reload.
evidence: take_player.js:1041 `if (Array.isArray(sp.fadeIds) && sp.fadeIds.length) fade(R, sp.fadeIds);` runs before :1044 `safety.clamp(...)`. fade() :789-790 records `hadOwn/prev` and sets `em2.filmHidden = true`. safety.js:249-259 `if (!em || ... hidden.has(em)) continue; ... prev: em.filmHidden, hadOwn: ... ; em.filmHidden = true;`. particles_query.js:335 drops filmHidden emitters only when the snapshot is rebuilt (the snapshot is cached per frame key). take_player.js:1395-1397 `fades = restoreFades(R); ... safety.release();`.
suggestedFix: Undo in reverse order of application: call `safety.release()` before `restoreFades(R)` in execute()'s finally. Or keep a single owner of `filmHidden` per emitter (a shared refcount/map) so neither restorer writes back a value the other set.
fixes:
Main fix, in safety.js `updateLens`: do not take over an emitter that something else has already hidden.

`if (!em || typeof em !== "object" || hidden.has(em) || em.filmHidden === true) continue;`

This matches particles_query's own skip of hidden emitters, and the pilot fade then remains the only owner of that flag.

Belt and braces, both optional:
- In take_player.js `fade()`, call `pq.invalidate()` (when it exists) after setting `em2.filmHidden = true`, so later queries in the same frame see the change.
- In `execute()`'s finally block, undo in reverse order of application: call `safety.release()` before `restoreFades(R)`.

title: ShotContext.sun is never provided, so solver light intents and sun-based classic placements are silently ignored
description: solver.js scores `intent.light` ('front'|'back'|'rim') and 'sun in frame' against `ctx.sun`, and classic.js frontBearing/side selection falls back to `ctx.sun.h`. Neither scout() nor resolveTake() ever sets `ctx.sun`, so a director's `intent: {light:'back'}` produces placements that ignore the light, with no warning. The sun is available on the page: `liveScene3d.skyLightingController._lastState.dirHeading/dirPitch`, in degrees and in the convention loop.js tickTerrainSunDir uses (direction toward the sun, compass heading).
failureScenario: scout({technique:'classic.establishing', intent:{light:'back'}}) at golden hour returns candidates ranked without any light term. The chosen shot is front-lit, although the plan asked for a backlit silhouette.
evidence: film/index.js:615 `const ctx = { ...resolved.ctx, groundZ: ... };` (no sun). resolveTake() builds ctx without sun. solver.js:206-212 `/** Valid ctx.sun above the horizon (outdoors), else null. */ const s = c.sun;`. loop.js:1400-1408 reads `state.dirHeading`/`state.dirPitch` (degrees) from `scene3d.skyLightingController?._lastState`.
suggestedFix: In resolveTake() (and therefore in scout/prepare), set `ctx.sun = {h: st.dirHeading*DEG, p: st.dirPitch*DEG}` from `live.skyLightingController?._lastState` when finite and outdoors. Report `sun: null` in the scout output when it is unavailable, so the director knows light intents were not scored.

title: setParticleCullConfig / allParticleManagers are never handed to the film runtime, so emitters stay RP6-culled for up to 5 film frames after cuts and whip pans
description: The RP6 cull is camera-relative, so a film camera far from the player still sees nearby particles. But it re-evaluates only every `recheckInterval` = 6 ticks. Under the stepped clock each film frame is one tick, so after an in-take cut (`traj.meta.cuts` → setCutCell) or a classic.whip-pan, emitters entering the frustum stay culled (they emit nothing and are hidden) for up to 5 recorded frames, about 167 ms at 30 fps. The seam built for this (SPEC §4.5, 'recheckInterval 1 … so no emitter stays frozen after a cut') has no caller, because page modules may not import particle_manager.js and the install site passes only {liveScene3d, THREE, sessionHandle, wasmExports}.
failureScenario: A concatenated drone plan with a cut bridge, or a whip-pan across a row of torches: the torches' flames pop in 1–5 frames after they enter the frame in the recorded take.
evidence: index.js:4529-4535 `m.installFilmMode({ liveScene3d, THREE, sessionHandle: liveScene3d.sessionHandle, wasmExports: liveScene3d.wasmExports })`. particle_manager.js:171 `recheckInterval: 6` and :2201 `const recheck = (this._rp6Frame % _RP6.recheckInterval) === 0;`. `rg 'setParticleCullConfig|allParticleManagers' scene3d/film` has no code hits.
suggestedFix: At the index.js install site, load the already-resident module (`import("./particles/particle_manager.js")` inside the `filmMode === "on"` branch, which is the same instance and still zero-cost when the flag is off) and pass `{particleCull: {setParticleCullConfig, allParticleManagers}}` in deps. Have take_player set `{recheckInterval: 1}` for the duration of a take, restore the returned previous config in its finally, and pass `allParticleManagers` to particles_query `managers`.
fixes:
In scene3d/index.js, inside the existing `filmMode === "on"` branch, load both modules together and pass the particle seams in. The module resolves to the same instance entities.js and statics.js already loaded, and nothing changes when the flag is off.

`Promise.all([import("./film/index.js"), import("./particles/particle_manager.js")]).then(([m, pm]) => m.installFilmMode({ liveScene3d, THREE, sessionHandle: liveScene3d.sessionHandle, wasmExports: liveScene3d.wasmExports, particleCull: { setParticleCullConfig: pm.setParticleCullConfig, allParticleManagers: pm.allParticleManagers } }))`

In film/index.js, forward `d.particleCull`:
- Give `createWorldQuery`/`createParticlesQuery` `managers: () => d.particleCull.allParticleManagers()`.
- Give `createTakePlayer` `particleCull: d.particleCull`.

In take_player `execute()`, just before the pre-roll:
- Set `R.prevCull = particleCull?.setParticleCullConfig?.({ recheckInterval: 1 })`, wrapped in try/catch.
- In the existing `finally`, call `setParticleCullConfig(R.prevCull)`.
This makes every rehearsed or recorded frame, including frames after in-take cuts and whip-pans, re-run the cull against the current film camera.

Update SEAMS.md and the README row from 'unused' to describe this wiring. Add a node test that asserts take_player sets recheckInterval to 1 for the take and restores the previous value afterwards.

1. **index.js install site.** Inside the existing `filmMode === "on"` branch, inject the module the page already has. Native ESM gives the same instance, and nothing loads when the flag is off:
   `Promise.all([import("./film/index.js"), import("./particles/particle_manager.js")]).then(([m, pm]) => m.installFilmMode({ liveScene3d, THREE, sessionHandle: liveScene3d.sessionHandle, wasmExports: liveScene3d.wasmExports, particleCull: { setParticleCullConfig: pm.setParticleCullConfig, allParticleManagers: pm.allParticleManagers } }))`

2. **film/index.js.** Keep `d.particleCull` only if `setParticleCullConfig` is a function. Pass it to `createTakePlayer({ ..., particleCull })`. Use it in `renderStills` too.

3. **take_player.js.** In `runStepped`, `runRealtime` and the rehearse path, before the pre-roll:
   `const prevCull = particleCull ? particleCull.setParticleCullConfig({ recheckInterval: 1 }) : null;`
   Restore it with `particleCull.setParticleCullConfig(prevCull)` in the existing `finally`.
   Optionally also raise `maxDistance`, so aerial or establishing shots more than 220 m from emitters are not distance-culled.

4. **renderStills.** Set `recheckInterval: 1` around the candidate loop and restore it in its `finally`, so every scout still re-evaluates the cull on the frame it captures.

5. **particles_query.** Optionally pass `allParticleManagers` to its `managers` option, so queries see every registered manager. Its current facade lookup finds the world and static managers.

6. **Test.** Add a case to tests/film_hooks.test.mjs or tests/film_runtime_camera.test.mjs: a fake `particleCull` records the set and restore calls around a stepped take and around a scout. Check that `recheckInterval` is 1 during the take and back to 6 afterwards, including when the take throws.

title: dispose() during a running take never releases the camera and removes the only API that could
description: dispose() aborts the take but skips `cameraOwner.release()` when `busy` is set. It then deletes `window.__film` and drops the INSTALLED entry. The take finishes asynchronously, but nothing releases the camera afterwards, so the positionCamera wrapper stays installed with `state.owned = true` and the follow camera stays frozen at the last film pose. A re-install creates a new owner that wraps the old wrapper, so releasing it does not unfreeze the camera either. dispose() also leaves the look (fog, grade, sky time, DoF) and any film avatar hide in place.
failureScenario: The CLI's emergency cleanup calls __film.dispose() mid-shoot. The take aborts, and the person who later opens that browser on the 1070 finds the game camera stuck at a film pose, with no __film to call release().
evidence: film/index.js:895-903 `takePlayer.abort(); ... try { if (!busy) cameraOwner.release(); } ... disposed = true; INSTALLED.delete(live); ... delete win.__film;`. camera_owner.js:458-467: the wrapper keeps re-asserting while `state.owned && state.wrapper === wrapper`.
suggestedFix: Make dispose() async, or schedule cleanup after the running take settles. Await the busy operation (or the take player's run promise), then call `cameraOwner.dispose()` (release + remove hooks), `look.restore()`, `world.avatar(true)` / `entityManager.clearAllFilmHidden()` and `cleanFrame.restore()`, and only then delete `window.__film`.
fixes:
In installFilmMode (scene3d/film/index.js):
(1) In exclusive(), keep the promise for the operation in progress (`let current = null; … const p = (async () => { busy = name; try { return await fn(); } finally { busy = null; current = null; } })(); current = p; return p;`).
(2) In shootImpl, rehearse and scout, after `await ready()` and before calling the take player, check `if (disposed) throw new FilmError("film mode was disposed", "FILM_DISPOSED")`. This way a dispose() during the start window really stops the take, because takePlayer.abort() is a no-op while run is null and execute() resets abortRequested.
(3) Rewrite dispose() as: `disposed = true; takePlayer.abort(); const finish = () => { try { cameraOwner.dispose(); } catch (_) {} try { cleanFrame.restore(); } catch (_) {} try { look.restore(); } catch (_) {} }; if (current) current.then(finish, finish); else finish();`. Then do INSTALLED.delete and remove window.__film as now. cameraOwner.dispose() releases the camera (unwrapping positionCamera) and drops liveScene3d.film. Returning `{ok:true, disposed:true, deferred: !!current}` keeps dispose() synchronous and JSON-safe.

title: The camera stays owned with the previous site's pose and filmViewer cell across world.teleport, which skews viewer-indoor and sealed-dungeon state until the next take
description: After a take the camera stays owned (nothing releases it between shots), and `live.filmViewer = {cell}` keeps the last take's cell. cells.js uses that cell as the viewer cell (`setViewerCell` plus `isIndoor = isIndoorCellId(viewer)` when it differs from the player cell) through the next teleport, world.ready and world.prewarm. Example: the previous site was outdoors and the next is a sealed dungeon. The stale outdoor cell makes `isIndoor` false, so `_sealedEvictLbKey` stays 0, and world.prewarm (which checks `live._sealedEvictLbKey`) bakes and populates up to 49 outdoor landblocks around the dungeon points. The first cut of the next take then evicts them all again with the sealed purge. Recorded frames are correct (the pre-roll cut re-seeds the cell), but prewarm and ready waste minutes of streaming work.
failureScenario: A plan that shoots Holtburg outdoors, then the Town Network. The prewarm at the dungeon site streams outdoor terrain, statics and buildings it does not need (sealed=false because of the stale outdoor film cell), and the first pre-roll triggers a mass eviction.
evidence: camera_owner.js:336-338 publishCell keeps `live.filmViewer` while owned. cells.js:2874-2880 a non-zero filmCell overrides the viewer cell. cells.js:3029-3031 `isIndoor = cellId !== 0 && viewerCell !== cellId ? isIndoorCellId(viewerCell) : playerIndoor`. cells.js:3413-3415 `_sealedEvictLbKey = sealed && ... ? ... : 0`. world.js:638-640 `const sealed = !!live._sealedEvictLbKey; const outdoorKinds = sealed ? [] : ["terrain","statics","buildings"];`. world.teleport (world.js:297) does not touch the camera owner.
suggestedFix: Have world.teleport() (or the API wrapper around it) park the film viewer: call a new `cameraOwner.parkCell()` that deletes `live.filmViewer` and sets pendingReseed until the next write, or release the camera on teleport and re-own in prepare. The player-head walk then drives the viewer cell while the site loads.
fixes: Add `parkCell()` to camera_owner. It sets `state.cell = 0`, `state.cellEye = null`, `state.pendingCut = 0` and `state.pendingReseed = true`, then calls publishCell(), which deletes `live.filmViewer` because cell is 0. Inject the cameraOwner (or just a `parkViewerCell` callback) into createWorld in film/index.js, and call it in world.teleport() right after send() succeeds. While the camera is parked, cells.js falls back to the player-head walk, so the dungeon's sealed state and `_sealedEvictLbKey` take effect during ready and prewarm. The next take's pre-roll setCutCell then re-seeds the cell as it does today. Optionally also move the owned pose to the player head, or clear state.pose, so the parked camera does not keep rendering the old site. Add a test: own, write, teleport, and assert that `live.filmViewer` is absent and `viewerCell() === 0`.

1. Add `parkCell()` to the object createCameraOwner returns (camera_owner.js). It sets `state.cell = 0`, `state.cellEye = null`, `state.pendingCut = 0` and `state.pendingReseed = true`, then calls `publishCell()`, which deletes `live.filmViewer` because cell is 0.
