title: Realtime takes grab a frame on every animation frame, but the mux assumes a constant timeline fps, so footage plays at the wrong speed (known gap 7 is a real defect)
description: In capture.mode "realtime", runRealtime arms a grab on every requestAnimationFrame callback (`R.armed = { t }`). Nothing decimates or duplicates frames to R.fps. recorder.grab() encodes each armed frame with timestamp t. For the default avc codec, drain.mjs writes the chunks as a raw Annex-B .h264, which keeps no timestamps. shoot.mjs then muxes with `muxArgv({..., fps})`, where `fps = timeline.fps`, and ffmpeg.mjs:145 builds `-r <fps> -i take.h264 -c copy`. Every realtime frame is therefore stamped 1/fps apart whatever the real display rate was. The JPEG 'frames' fallback has the same problem (`-framerate <fps> -i %06d.jpg`). The report's `durationSec: raw.frames / fps` repeats the error. edl.mjs:155 counts the take's available frames by index at the timeline fps, so a realtime take that is short on frames cannot fill its edit. The only signal is a warning: 'drained N frames, planned M'.
failureScenario: SPEC §0 measures 22–31 fps real time on the 1070, and SPEC says shots whose subject moves (NPCs, the avatar) use capture.mode:'realtime'. Take a 10 s realtime take at fps 30 that renders at about 25 fps: it yields about 250 frames. Muxed at -r 30, it plays in 8.3 s, so the NPC walks 1.2x too fast and drifts off the song's beats. The EDL expected takeFrames = 300, so the edit runs out of footage. Irregular rAF intervals (22–31 fps) also become visible speed judder. If the display loop ever runs at 60 Hz, the same take becomes 2x slow motion.
evidence: take_player.js:1300-1308 (realtime loop): `if (R.armed) R.dropped += 1; ... else { R.armed = { t }; }`, run on every rAF with no 1/fps boundary test. recorder.js:429-466 `grab(filmTimeSec)` → `new Frame(canvas, { timestamp: ts, duration: frameDurUs })`, one encode per grab. drain.mjs:8 `avc → <name>.h264 raw Annex-B bytes, concatenated exactly as encoded`. shoot.mjs:233 `const fps = timeline.fps;` and :291 `muxArgv({ kind: raw.kind, input: raw.path, output: file, fps, container: ext })`. ffmpeg.mjs:145 `["-hide_banner", "-y", "-r", r, "-i", input, "-c", "copy", ...]`. shoot.mjs:308 `durationSec: raw.frames / fps`. Found by reading the code; it cannot be run without a browser.
suggestedFix: Make realtime capture constant-rate in the page. Keep a frame counter n and arm a grab only when wall-relative t >= n/fps. When a callback skips past one or more boundaries, re-grab that frame for each one it skipped. Stamp each VideoFrame with n/fps·1e6, not the raw t. Alternatively, keep the real timestamps: write them out, for example as an mkv timecodes file, or mux avc through a container that carries pts, then resample to the timeline fps (`-vf fps=<fps>`) at assembly. Either way, report durationSec from the real timestamps.
fixes:
Make realtime capture constant-rate in the page (scene3d/film/runtime/take_player.js runRealtime + installGrab).

1. Keep a per-run counter `R.nextGrab = 0`.
2. In onFrame, set `R.armed = { t }` as now, but make the grab in postRender step through timeline frames:
   - compute `due = Math.floor(a.t * R.fps + 1e-6)` (the last timeline frame index whose time is ≤ t);
   - for each n from R.nextGrab to due, call `R.recorder.grab(n / R.fps)`. That is one VideoFrame per crossed boundary, and all of them can come from the same canvas inside the same postRender, because preserveDrawingBuffer is false;
   - then set `R.nextGrab = due + 1`;
   - if due < R.nextGrab (the display runs faster than fps), skip the grab and do not count it as dropped.
3. Duplicates are capped by the backpressure check, and are counted in a new `R.duplicated` stat.
4. At the end, grab up to `round(R.endT * R.fps)` so the take holds exactly takeFrames frames.
5. Report `durationSec = grabbed / R.fps` and `realtime: {wallSec: R.endT, displayFrames: k, duplicated, skipped}`.

After this, the avc `-r fps -c copy` mux, the frames `-framerate` mux and the EDL frame-index math are all correct unchanged. Only the take player changes, and the VP9 IVF pts (round(ts·fps/1e6)) become exact integers.

Alternative, Node-only: keep the wall timestamps. Write every chunk's timestampUs to a sidecar file. Mux avc to mkv with real pts (for example `-use_wallclock_as_timestamps` is not viable, so use the mkvmerge timestamp file or `-f h264 … -bsf:v setts=pts=…` driven by the sidecar), then resample with `-vf fps=<fps>` (re-encode). Report frames as `round((lastTs - firstTs)/1e6 * fps) + 1`.

Add a unit test: a realtime take at fps 30 on a 26 Hz and on a 60 Hz fake display must both encode exactly 30·D frames with timestamps k/30.

Make realtime capture constant-rate in the page, so everything downstream (raw Annex-B, `-r fps` mux, EDL frame indices, `durationSec = frames/fps`) stays correct without CLI changes:

- **runRealtime (take_player.js):** keep `n` = the next output frame index. On each rAF, compute `due = floor(t*fps + 1e-6) + 1 - n`, the number of 1/fps boundaries crossed since the last grab.
  - If `due <= 0` (display faster than fps), do not arm, and do not count a drop.
  - Otherwise arm `R.armed = { t: n/fps, repeat: due }` and advance `n += due`.
- **recorder.grab(filmTimeSec, repeat = 1):** build one VideoFrame from the canvas, synchronously as now. Encode it, then for each extra repeat encode `new VideoFrame(frame, { timestamp: ts + i*frameDurUs, duration: frameDurUs })` and close each clone. A skipped boundary becomes a held frame on the fps grid. For the 'frames' kind, push the same JPEG once per repeat.
- **Take end:** stop when `n >= round(D*fps)`, so a realtime take yields exactly takeFrames.
- **Telemetry:** count the duplicated frames (e.g. `R.held`) in the report.
- **Test:** update the test at tests/film_runtime_capture.test.mjs:1108-1125 to expect 10 frames at fps 10 for both the 20 Hz and 5 Hz displays.

Alternative CLI-side fix: keep the drained per-chunk `timestampUs`, write a timecode file, or mux through a container that carries pts. Then retime to `timeline.fps` with `-vf fps=<fps>` at assembly, and report `durationSec` from `(lastTimestampUs - firstTimestampUs)/1e6 + 1/fps` rather than `frames/fps`.

Preferred, exact constant rate in the page:
- In runRealtime, keep a film-frame counter n and compute the target index `m = floor(t*fps + 1e-6)`.
- Arm a grab only when m >= n, and carry `repeat = m - n + 1` to cover boundaries the callback skipped. Arm nothing when the display runs faster than fps.
- In recorder.grab, encode the canvas VideoFrame once stamped n/fps·1e6. For each extra repeat, encode `new VideoFrame(frame, {timestamp: (n+j)/fps·1e6})`, or push the same JPEG again for 'frames'. Then set n = m + 1.
- Frames dropped for backpressure should also advance n, so the timeline stays wall-locked.
- Then raw.frames ≈ D·fps and the existing `-r fps` mux, durationSec and EDL frame indexing are correct.
- Update test T1: a 20 Hz display at fps 10 should give 10 frames stamped 0.1 s apart.

Minimal CLI-only alternative, which fixes average speed but not jitter:
- In shoot.mjs, for `mode === 'realtime'` with raw.kind avc or frames and raw.frames > 1, measure `rate = (raw.frames - 1) * 1e6 / (raw.lastTimestampUs - raw.firstTimestampUs)`.
- Pass `fps: rate` to muxArgv. Decimal -r and -framerate values are accepted.
- Report `fps: rate`, `durationSec: raw.frames / rate`, and expected frames as `round(takeDuration * rate)`.
- edl.mjs already maps source frames through `tfps = take.fps`, and the assembly `fps=F` filter resamples to the timeline rate.
- Better still, have the sink write per-frame timestamps, for example a timecode file, so the jitter can be resampled exactly.

title: look.fog restarts the retail ~20 s wall-clock fog roll-in at every prepare, so every fog take drifts from clear to foggy (known gap 6 is a real defect)
description: prepare() re-applies the whole merged look for every take (index.js:795 `look.apply(take.look)`). The fog setter always stores a new object: `lookFogOverride()` returns `{ option, ...LOOK_FOG_ROWS[opt] }`, then `win.__environFogOverride = o`. environ_override.js treats a new object identity as a new AdminEnvirons message and restarts the transition at 0. It then rolls the fog in over 25 ticks of 0.8 s, about 20 s, on retailLightNowSec(), which is performance.now() wall time. Nothing in the film runtime pins, pre-rolls or film-clocks that transition. The film boot URL (session.mjs buildFilmUrl) does not pass `environRetail=off`, the documented snap-on escape. Fog density inside a take therefore changes over the shot. In stepped capture it follows wall time per encoded frame, not film time, so rehearse and shoot show different fog and a locked replay does not reproduce the look.
failureScenario: A plan with look.fog:'white' on a site, and three 4 s shots there. Each prepare() writes a fresh override, so each take opens nearly fog-free and thickens during recording. The pre-roll is about 0.25 s plus site.settleSec, far short of the ~20 s needed. Cutting between the takes jumps from thick fog at the end of shot 1 to clear air at the start of shot 2. In a stepped 1080p take that runs slower than real time, the roll-in completes after a different number of frames than in the rehearsal.
evidence: look.js:69-75 `export function lookFogOverride(name) { ... return { option: opt, ...LOOK_FOG_ROWS[opt] }; }` and look.js:211-215 `set(v) { ... const o = lookFogOverride(v); win.__environFogOverride = o; ...}`. index.js:793-795 `// The take's look ... is applied once the take is valid: the WHOLE look ... const lookResult = isObj(take.look) ? look.apply(take.look) : null;`. environ_override.js:20-31 `25 fog ticks of 0.8 s ... => the fog rolls in over ~20 s ... a new object identity is a new message, so the transition restarts at 0`. retail_light_tick.js:58-62 `retailLightNowSec() { return performance.now() * 0.001 ...}`. session.mjs:58-62: the boot query has no environRetail param. `grep -rn 'environRetail\|retailLight' scene3d/film tools/film` returns no hits.
suggestedFix: In look.js, reuse the current override object when the fog option is unchanged; return early if `win.__environFogOverride?.option === opt`. Then also either add `environRetail=off` to buildFilmUrl, so film fog snaps on deterministically, or have prepare() report fog as 'settling' and make the CLI wait out the transition (or extend preRollSec) before recording. Long term, drive the environ transition from the film clock during stepped takes, as is already done for the scenery and FX time sources.
fixes:
1) In scene3d/film/runtime/look.js fog.set(): make it idempotent. Resolve the option, then if `win.__environFogOverride && win.__environFogOverride.option === opt`, keep the existing object and return `{ok:true, value: name}` without reassigning it. This stops later takes at a site from restarting the fade. Update the film_runtime_world test assertion at :152 to match.

2) Make the first application deterministic by adding `&environRetail=off` to buildFilmUrl in tools/film/lib/session.mjs. With that flag the override snaps on in the next frame, with no wall-clock fade (loop.js:2047-2062 path), so rehearse and shoot match. Alternatively, keep the retail fade and have prepare() report `fog: {settling: true, settleSec: 20}`, with shoot.mjs waiting it out before the first take after a fog change.

3) Optional, longer term: let the film clock drive the environOverride `now` during stepped takes, as it already does for the scenery and FX time sources.

title: Pilot 'fade' does nothing for static occluders (trees, static props), the main soft-occluder case, because no static id reaches fadeIds and the statics.js __filmHidden seam is never used (known gap 1 is partly real)
description: Gap 1 is resolved for entities and particle clouds: sensors.js collects `occluderIds` (rig guids and particle keys), mapper.js turns `fade` into fadeIds, and take_player.fade() and restoreFades() hide and restore them through setFilmHidden and emitter.filmHidden. Static occluders are not covered. describeHit() resolves scenery and statics hits to a kind and a did but leaves guid null. sensors therefore pushes nothing for them, because only `rec.guid !== null` hits are added. The pilot is still told that trees and props are soft occluders the runtime 'can fade', and the code policy maps soft to fade. When the subject is hidden behind a tree, both JEV and the code pilot choose `fade`. fadeIds comes out empty, and `reroute` is false because the choice was fade. take_player.fade() handles only numeric guids and string particle keys. No film code ever sets the `userData.__filmHidden` marker that statics.js cullStaticsGroup was changed to honour (SPEC §4.4).
failureScenario: A drone.orbit-poi around an NPC in Holtburg, where a tree trunk passes between the camera and the subject. The sensors report visibility 'hidden' and occluded_by 'tree'. The pilot answers occluder_action = fade, which is correct per its criteria and is also the policy_code answer. mapper sets `fadeIds = []` and `reroute = false`. The camera holds its line and the subject stays hidden for the whole occlusion, with neither a fade nor a reroute. A static prop such as a cart or barrel behaves the same way.
evidence: sensors.js:743 `if (rec.guid !== null && !occIds.includes(rec.guid)) occIds.push(rec.guid);`. world_query.js:899-905 (static branch of describeHit): sets only `refined` and `did`; `guid` stays null. sense_words.js:208-209 `soft: ["tree", "prop", "particles"]`. questions.js:275 `soft = ... (foliage, small props, smoke or fire clouds — the film runtime can fade them out)`. mapper.js:488-489 `sp.fadeIds = occChoice === "fade" ? occluderIds(sf, limits.maxFadeIds) : []; sp.reroute = occChoice === "reroute";`. take_player.js:759-792: fade() has number (setFilmHidden) and string (particle snapshot key) branches only. `grep -rn '__filmHidden\|setVisibleAt' scene3d/film` returns 0 hits, yet statics.js:4579 honours `ud.__filmHidden === true`.
suggestedFix: Give static hits a fadeable id and apply it. Have world_query.describeHit or staticsNear return the static's three node (or `{node, batch, instanceId}`), and have sensors push a string key such as `static:<lbKey>:<index>`. In take_player.fade(), resolve that key and set `node.userData.__filmHidden = true` for Mesh, InstancedMesh and LOD, or use `setVisibleAt(i, false)` for BatchedMesh instances; restore both in restoreFades(). As a minimum safety net, in mapper.js fall back to `reroute = true` when the choice is 'fade' and occluderIds(sf) is empty.
fixes:
Minimum v1 fix in scene3d/film/pilot/mapper.js apply(): compute `const ids = occChoice === "fade" ? occluderIds(sf, limits.maxFadeIds) : [];`, set `sp.fadeIds = ids;` and set `sp.reroute = occChoice === "reroute" || (occChoice === "fade" && ids.length === 0);`. A soft occluder with no fadeable identity (scenery tree, static prop) then falls back to the existing take_player updateReroute bias instead of doing nothing. Add a test in tests/film_pilot_loop or film_perception: a scenery-trunk occluder gives fade, empty ids and reroute true.

Optional full fix later: have describeHit/staticsNear return a per-instance handle, `{node, instanceId}`, and push a `static:<lbKey>:<index>` key from sensors. take_player.fade() would hide only that instance: BatchedMesh.setVisibleAt(id, false), or a zeroed instance matrix for an InstancedMesh with the old matrix saved. Use `userData.__filmHidden` plus `visible = false` only for singleton Mesh/LOD nodes, never for a shared InstancedMesh/BatchedMesh, and restore all of it in restoreFades().

Two layers.

1. **Required, small safety net (mapper.js around line 488).** Compute `const ids = occChoice === "fade" ? occluderIds(sf, limits.maxFadeIds) : [];`, then set `sp.fadeIds = ids;` and `sp.reroute = occChoice === "reroute" || (occChoice === "fade" && ids.length === 0);`. With this, a fade that has no fadeable target falls back to the existing take_player reroute bias instead of doing nothing. Add a test: a scenery trunk occluder must give reroute === true.

2. **Real static fade.** Have describeHit's static branch, or staticsNear, return a fadeable handle such as `{node, batch, instanceId}` keyed by a string like `static:<lbKey>:<index>`, and have sensors.js push that key into occIds. In take_player.fade(), resolve the key:
   - For a top-level staticsGroup Mesh, InstancedMesh or LOD, set `userData.__filmHidden = true` and `visible = false`, as SEAMS.md:25 specifies.
   - For a BatchedMesh, call `setVisibleAt(iid, false)`.
   
   Record the previous values and restore them in restoreFades().

   Scenery is likely batched or instanced per landblock. If only a whole-node hide is possible, skip the fade (it would hide many trees) and let fix 1 reroute instead.

title: The 'FULL DATA' check reports [PASS] while asserting nothing when the real gazetteer inputs are missing (a skip disguised as a pass)
description: checkAsync('FULL DATA: > 3,000 sites ...') returns early with a 'note:' line when any real input is absent, and still counts as passed. That is the case in the CI js job (holtburger-ci.yml runs `node harness/run-js-headless.mjs --quiet` on ubuntu, where /mnt/wbterminal2 and ~/projects/RetailSmoke do not exist) and on any other box. The harness has two rules for exactly this: a suite that asserts nothing must not count as a pass (F5, `--allow-skips` is off by default), and a suite that needs local data declares `requires` so it shows as NO-FIXTURE. SPEC §6 also forbids SKIP banners. This check avoids both: it does not use the word SKIP and is counted in 'N passed'. Gate readiness otherwise checked out in this dimension. All 32 in-scope film suites passed standalone in 0.1–6.4 s each, one at a time. The other checks also passed: --coverage (0 unregistered), test_suite_hygiene, test_gate_browser_smokes, lint-url-flags (and --strict), audit-flag-defaults, lint-event-consumers, gen-modulepreload --check (423 modules, unchanged), no new Worker sites, no top-level await, and an esbuild browser bundle of scene3d/film/index.js. lint-harness-params fails on 4 params, but the same 4 fail at HEAD, so that is not caused by film. 51 existing suites touching the seam files also passed.
failureScenario: Run the gate in CI or on the 1070: film_sites prints 'note: real gazetteer inputs not on this machine ... full-data build not run' and then '[PASS] FULL DATA ...', reporting 30 passed. If the full build regresses (fewer than 3,000 sites, duplicate towns, missing teleports), every machine without the data keeps passing, and the report never shows that the check did not run.
evidence: tests/film_sites.test.mjs:492-498: `await checkAsync("FULL DATA: ...", async () => { const need = [...]; const absent = need.filter((k) => !fs.existsSync(DEFAULT_PATHS[k])); if (absent.length) { console.log(`    note: real gazetteer inputs not on this machine (...) — full-data build not run`); return; } ...`. checkAsync counts any non-throwing fn as passed. Executed: `node --max-old-space-size=1536 tests/film_sites.test.mjs` printed 30 passed in 3.05 s; on this laptop the data exists, so it ran: 'full build: 3452 sites ... in 2238 ms'.
suggestedFix: Move the full-data check into its own suite (for example tests/film_sites_full.test.mjs) and register it in TIER5 with `requires: <one gazetteer input path>`, so the runner reports NO-FIXTURE when the data is absent. Or keep it here, exclude it from the passed count when the data is absent, and print it as an explicitly not-run line.

title: One incomplete world.prewarm aborts the whole shoot (all remaining sites and shots)
description: shootSchedule calls world.prewarm with a non-soft filmCallWith, outside the per-shot try/catch. The page's prewarm returns {ok:false, timedOut:true, missing:{…}} whenever any landblock is not baked inside its 30 s default. filmCallWith turns ok:false into a FilmCliError (exit 1), and that error escapes shootSchedule. Prewarm is only an optimisation: the readiness gate has already passed. Even so, one slow or evicted landblock ends the whole schedule. Known gap 8 (prewarmed landblocks outside the player ring are the first LRU victims) makes such a timeout likely on the 1070.
failureScenario: Timeline with sites A, B, C. Site A teleports and passes ready, then prewarm times out because one corridor landblock was evicted again. `film shoot --all` (and `run`) throws out of shootSchedule with exit 1. A, B and C shoot nothing, no failures list or reports are written, and the long run is lost.
evidence: Code: `if (entry.prewarm) await filmCallWith(page, { timeoutMs: 300_000 }, "world.prewarm", entry.prewarm);` (no soft, no catch). world.js prewarm sets `report.ok = !report.timedOut`. Probe /tmp/claude-1000/probe/prewarm.mjs: fake page whose prewarm returns the real timed-out shape → `shootSchedule THREW: FILM_CALL_FAILED 1 __film.world.prewarm failed: {"ok":false,"timedOut":true…`; page calls: `world.teleport @telepoi A → world.ready → world.prewarm` (sites B and C never visited).
suggestedFix: Call prewarm with {soft:true}. Log the report's missing landblocks as a warning and append them to shoot-log.jsonl, then continue with the site's shots (optionally retry the prewarm once). Only a hard error such as NO_FILM should abort.

title: Realtime takes are muxed at constant timeline fps: wrong speed, short takes, frozen frames in the edit
description: Realtime takes grab one frame per requestAnimationFrame at the wall clock (take_player runRealtime; recorder.grab(t) with real timestamps). That rate is 22–31 fps on the 1070, or the display rate. The drain sink records firstTimestampUs and lastTimestampUs, but muxArgv('avc') ignores them: `-r <timeline fps> -i take.h264 -c copy` re-times every frame to 1/fps. The take report then sets frames = drained count and durationSec = frames / fps. The take therefore plays fast (or slow at a 60 Hz rAF), and assembly sees it as short and pads it by holding the last frame. Server-driven motion, the reason realtime mode exists, plays at the wrong speed. The VP9 path behaves differently: IVF pts gaps make ffmpeg duplicate frames at `-r`, so the muxed frame count differs from report.frames. The `tpad` pad count in edl.mjs then over-pads and the program loses sync. Known gap 7 is a real v1 defect.
failureScenario: Shot with a moving actor (schema auto-selects capture realtime), takeDuration 4 s at 30 fps. The 1070 renders 25 fps, so 100 frames are drained. The mp4 lasts 3.33 s with motion 1.2× fast. assemble warns 'take s1 is 20 frame(s) short; its last frame is held' and the final cut shows a 0.67 s freeze.
evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-1000/probe/rtprobe.mjs: sink 100 chunks with timestamps 0..3.96 s → `raw avc frames 100 … real duration 4 s`; `mux argv: -hide_banner -y -r 30 -i …/s1.h264 -c copy … → muxed duration 3.333 s (speed × 1.20)`; buildAssembly → `take s1 is 20 frame(s) short; its last frame is held`, filter `tpad=stop_mode=clone:stop=20`. shoot.mjs:309-310 `frames: raw.frames, durationSec: raw.frames / fps`.
suggestedFix: For captureMode 'realtime', mux with the measured rate, measuredFps = (frames−1)·1e6/(lastTimestampUs−firstTimestampUs), via `-r measuredFps -i take.h264`. Then resample to constant fps by re-encoding with `-vf fps=<timeline fps>` (or pass the measured fps as takes[shot].fps so edl.mjs trims in the take's own rate). Read the take's frame count back with ffprobe instead of trusting the drained chunk count, for all kinds.

title: After a failed take the page take keeps running; the CLI then sends the next site's teleport mid-recording
description: When drainTake throws (a recorder.drain evaluate error, or the shoot evaluate exceeding evalBudgetMs = frames·500 ms + 300 s, which slow stepped JEV decisions of up to 15 s each can cause), or when mux fails, shootSchedule records the failure and continues. It never calls __film.abort() and never waits for the page to go idle. The page's take keeps running, so every following prepare fails with FILM_BUSY. Neither the CLI nor the page refuses a teleport while a take runs (index.js world.teleport has no busy guard), so the next site's teleport is sent while the page is still recording. That breaks the 'never record across a teleport' structure the module header claims, and the rest of the schedule is lost.
failureScenario: Site A shot a1: the third recorder.drain call fails with a CDP error. a1 is marked failed, a2's prepare returns 'film is busy', then `@telepoi Glenden Wood` is sent while a1 is still running in the page, and b1 fails busy as well.
evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-1000/probe/cascade.mjs (fake page whose take never ends unless aborted): `shoot started` / `warn: shot a1 failed: __film.recorder.drain failed…` / `prepare a2 → busy` / `teleport @telepoi Glenden Wood (page take running: true)` / `prepare b1 → busy`; failures: a1@take, a2@take, b1@take. No 'abort' call appears in film.mjs or shoot.mjs.
suggestedFix: On any error inside an attempt (drain, shoot, mux), call filmCallWith(page, {soft:true}, 'abort') and poll __film.status() until active === false and take.running === false before continuing. In shootSchedule, check that status().active is false before goAndWait, and refuse to teleport otherwise.

title: {bars:n} cuts land a beat early for every analysed song when the edit starts before the first downbeat
description: resolveEnd for {bars} keeps the length and snaps to the nearest BEAT whenever the shot does not start exactly on a bar line. The first shot starts at edit t=0, but analyze.mjs puts bars[0] on the first detected downbeat (e.g. 0.51 s; it only clamps a pre-bar starting within 5 % of a bar before 0). With the default song.offsetSec 0, shot 1 ends one beat before a downbeat. Each following contiguous {bars} shot then also starts mid-bar, so every bar cut in the film misses the downbeat until an explicit start re-aligns it. Cutting on bar lines is the stated purpose of {bars}.
failureScenario: Song analysed from a 120 BPM loop whose first downbeat is at 0.5 s. Plan shots: {bars:4}, {bars:4}, {bars:2} with offsetSec 0. The cuts land at 8.0, 16.03 and 20.03 s; the true downbeats are 8.5, 16.5 and 20.5 s.
evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-1000/probe/barsprobe.mjs (real analyzeSong): `first bars [0.5111, 2.5106, 4.5105]`; `s1 edit 0 → 8 cut on a true downbeat? false`, `s2 8 → 16.033333 false`, `s3 16.033333 → 20.033333 false`. The same happens on examplePlan with a synthetic grid (compprobe.mjs): s010 0→7.866667 (downbeat 8.37), s020…s050 all end on beat 4. Code: `const pos = grid.barPos(inT) + n; const posR = Math.round(pos); let t = Math.abs(pos - posR) < 1e-6 ? grid.barTime(posR) : grid.nearestBeat(grid.barTime(pos));`
suggestedFix: When inT precedes the first bar (barPos(inT) < 0), or for the first shot, count bars from the next downbeat so the pickup joins the shot: t = barTime(ceil(barPos(inT) − 1e-6) + n). Alternatively snap to the nearest downbeat whenever the shot started within a beat of a bar line. At minimum, default or warn to set song.offsetSec to the first downbeat.

title: --password ends up in the world-readable heavy-lock file /tmp/hb-heavy.lock/owner.json
description: withLock calls acquireHeavyLock for boot, run, shoot and the other commands. heavy_lock.mjs ownerRecord writes `cmd: [basename(argv[1]), ...process.argv.slice(2)].join(' ')` into /tmp/hb-heavy.lock/owner.json (mode 0664) for the whole run. If the job is killed by a signal, the file stays until the next heavy job reclaims it. The CLI's scrubber never sees this write. This breaks the owner decision ('the password is a run-time argument only — never in docs, plans, logs') and film.mjs's own claim that the password is scrubbed from every byte the CLI writes. SKILL.md and film-director.md both document `--password=…` as a supported form. The CLI tests miss it because they inject a fake acquireHeavyLock.
failureScenario: `node tools/film/film.mjs run my-video --password=hunter2` keeps `{"cmd":"film.mjs run my-video --password=hunter2"…}` in /tmp/hb-heavy.lock/owner.json, readable by every local user and process, for the hours of the shoot.
evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-1000/probe/lockleak.mjs (real acquireHeavyLock with dir under /tmp/claude-1000, process.argv emulating `film.mjs boot --password=hunter2secret`): owner.json = `{"pid":…,"cmd":"film.mjs boot --password=hunter2secret --assume-muted","label":"film boot",…}`, file mode 664. heavy_lock.mjs:176 builds cmd from process.argv.
suggestedFix: In main() (or before every acquire), rewrite process.argv entries that start with `--password=` to `--password=[redacted]`, since heavy_lock reads process.argv when it acquires. Or add an explicit `cmd` option to acquireHeavyLock and pass the scrubbed argv. Also warn that FILM_PASSWORD is preferred.

title: Stepped rehearsal runs with the previous shot's realtime JEV limits
description: In shootOne the attempt-0 rehearsal (always stepped) runs before `o.broker?.setDecideOptions?.(DECIDE_OPTIONS[mode])` at line 260. The broker still holds whatever options the previous shot set. After a realtime shot that is {timeoutMs:1200, maxRetries:0}, while the page's stepped bridge waits up to 15 s. JEV calls in the rehearsal time out and fall back to the code policy, and in --locked mode that rehearsal becomes the replayed camera path.
failureScenario: Schedule order: realtime shot s1, then fpv shot s2 (auto-rehearsed). s2's rehearsal decisions slower than 1.2 s fail with kind 'timeout', so telemetry shows source 'code' and the --locked replay flies a code-policy path.
evidence: shoot.mjs:253-258 rehearse/prepare, then line 260 `o.broker?.setDecideOptions?.(DECIDE_OPTIONS[mode]);`. DECIDE_OPTIONS.realtime = {timeoutMs:1200, maxRetries:0}; installBroker sets stepped only once.
suggestedFix: Call broker.setDecideOptions(DECIDE_OPTIONS.stepped) immediately before the rehearse call, then set DECIDE_OPTIONS[mode] before shoot.

title: A failing retake throws away an already-recorded earlier attempt
description: The attempt loop in shootOne has no per-attempt catch. If attempt 0 is recorded and judged 'confirm' (so a retake starts) and the retake then fails (prepare busy, drain error, mux failure), the exception leaves shootOne. reports/<shot>.json is never written, the shot is counted as a failure, `shoot` exits 1 and `run` stops before assemble, although a usable take exists.
failureScenario: Shot s1: attempt 0 is kept with band 'confirm', triggering a retake. The retake's ffmpeg mux fails. Result: `FAILED s1 at take`, no reports/s1.json, and `run` stops (exit 1).
evidence: shoot.mjs:242-336: `for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= o.retakes; attempt++) { … try { prepare/rehearse/shoot/drain } finally { avatar } … await runFfmpeg(…) … }` with no catch around an attempt. chooseAttempt and the report write (lines 338-347) are reached only when every attempt succeeds.
suggestedFix: Wrap each attempt in try/catch. On failure, log it, abort the page take (see the abort finding), and break. If any earlier attempt exists, run chooseAttempt and the report write on the attempts recorded so far.

title: frames/VP9 re-encode fails on an odd canvas size (libx264 yuv420p needs even dimensions)
description: The recorder's 'frames' fallback grabs `canvas.toDataURL('image/jpeg')` at whatever size the canvas has, not the even encoder size. muxArgv then encodes those JPEGs with `-c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p` and no scaling, and the VP9→mp4 path does the same. An odd canvas makes libx264 refuse to open, so every take fails at mux. The CLI only warns about the canvas/timeline size mismatch, and the SPEC's own measured window is 1280×633. This is part of known gap 9.
failureScenario: `film shoot … --codec=frames` on a page not booted by `film boot` (the CLI warns 'canvas follows the window size'), with the window at 1280×633. Every take fails with 'height not divisible by 2'.
evidence: Probe with real ffmpeg on 65×37 lavfi JPEGs in /tmp/claude-1000/probe/ff/odd: muxArgv({kind:'frames'}) → `exit 187 [libx264] width not divisible by 2 (65x37) | Error while opening encoder`. recorder.js grab(): `url = canvas.toDataURL("image/jpeg", jpegQ)` (canvas size).
suggestedFix: Add `-vf scale=trunc(iw/2)*2:trunc(ih/2)*2` (or `pad=ceil(iw/2)*2:ceil(ih/2)*2`) to the frames and vp9→mp4 argv. Or scale to the timeline width×height there, since assembly scales anyway.

title: `film go <site>` skips interior readiness for indoor (EnvCell) sites that have a map position
description: readyTargetsForSite sets interiorLb only when the site is indoor AND (map == null OR kind === 'dungeon'). Gazetteer towns and POIs whose exact @teleloc destination is an EnvCell carry a map position, so they get interiorLb null. Examples: Kor-Gursha 0x009C…, Crater Lake Village, Northwatch Castle, Freebooter Keep and 21 more. world.ready then never waits for envCellLoadedLbs or __interiorBuildPending. It gates on outdoor terrain of that landblock instead, which may never bake for a dungeon landblock. readyTargetsForCommand on the same teleport string does flag the interior, so the two derivations disagree.
failureScenario: `film go kor-gursha`, then `film scout`: ready reports ok before the underground cells are built, so the stills show void. Or it times out waiting on outdoor terrain of 0x009C0000.
evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-1000/probe/sitesprobe.mjs over the real 3,452-site build: 30 issues, all of the form `interior mismatch kor-gursha (town, indoor true, map true): cmd 10223616 site null`, `crater-lake-village … cmd 2429550592 site null`, `northwatch-castle (poi …)`.
suggestedFix: Derive interiorLb from the destination cell actually used. When teleport.best is an @teleloc, use readyTargetsForCommand(site.teleport.best). Otherwise set interiorLb whenever site.cell is an EnvCell ((cell & 0xFFFF) >= 0x100), regardless of map or kind.

title: boot opens and logs in a new tab without checking that its window is off-screen
description: The owner rule says film work on the 1070 never shows on screen. Only `browser check` inspects windowInfo, and in `run` that check happens before boot creates the tab. boot calls s.context.newPage(), sets the viewport, navigates and logs in without calling windowInfo or Browser.setWindowBounds. If Chrome places the new target in a new window (no normal window open, e.g. after the last off-screen window was closed while the CDP-enabled process stayed alive), the film page renders on the person's screen for the whole session.
failureScenario: The 1070 test Chrome has no open window. `film run proj` passes browser check (no film page, so no window finding), then boot's newPage opens a window at the default on-screen position and the world renders in front of the 1070's user.
evidence: film.mjs boot: `if (!page) { … page = await s.context.newPage(); }` followed by applyViewport, installBroker and page.goto, with no windowInfo call. windowInfo is referenced only in `browser check` (film.mjs:881-882).
suggestedFix: After newPage (and on --reuse), call windowInfo(s.context, page). If offScreen is false, call Browser.setWindowBounds({windowId, bounds:{left:-32000, top:-32000}}) and re-check, or refuse with exit 2 and close only the tab boot itself created.
